_comment: SDLC project configuration — used by `devaudit install` / `devaudit update` to generate CI workflows
_comment_host: Deploy host adapter under sdlc/files/hosts/ (railway, vercel, custom, ...). Chosen at `devaudit install --host <name>`; omit for railway. It decides which host-specific workflows and prerequisites are generated and checked. See docs/adding-a-host.md.
_comment_branches: Branch model the sdlc-implementer skill follows. integration_branch = where implementation PRs land and ci.yml uploads gate evidence on push. release_branch = the protected production branch the integration branch is promoted to via the UAT-approved release PR.
_comment_typescript_check_env: Optional env applied only to the TypeScript Check step — e.g. { "NODE_OPTIONS": "--max-old-space-size=4096" } for a project where `tsc --noEmit` OOMs at V8's default heap. Leave empty/absent for no env: block (default).
_comment_install_flags: Optional flags appended to `npm ci` in "Install dependencies" — e.g. "--legacy-peer-deps" for a project whose lockfile has a peer-dep mismatch npm can't resolve strictly. Leave empty for plain `npm ci` (default).
_comment_e2e_setup: Optional foreground command run before the dev server starts — use it to stand up a DISPOSABLE LOCAL database so the E2E gate never touches production. The consumer owns the command (the framework stays stack-agnostic). For a Supabase project: install the CLI, `supabase start`, load the local schema + seed, e.g. "supabase start && psql \"$DATABASE_URL\" -f supabase/schema-local.sql". Pair with e2e_env below to point the dev server + tests at the local stack. Leave empty for projects whose dev server already targets a safe test DB.
_comment_e2e_authenticated: Optional report-only authenticated e2e gate (continue-on-error, never blocks the merge). e2e_projects = Playwright project names that need a logged-in session (auth-setup runs automatically as their dependency); e2e_seed_command seeds admins/fixtures before the run. Author these specs with the e2e-test-engineer skill (evidenceShot per AC). Leave empty to run only the blocking smoke project above.
_comment_e2e_data: Test data (DevAudit-Installer#1116): declare where the tests get their data with e2e_data_isolation (none | ephemeral | shared_serialised | shared | unknown). When set (and not none), e2e-regression.yml runs scripts/e2e-data-lifecycle.sh around the tests: e2e_reset_command, then e2e_seed_command (files in e2e_seed_paths, tracked in version control), then e2e_preflight_command (non-zero fails the run); after the tests a best-effort e2e_reset_command, then e2e_leak_check_command (last line = rows left behind) and the e2e_max_skipped budget. feature_e2e_projects limits the feature-PR run to the listed Playwright projects. Unset keeps today's behaviour, even with e2e_seed_command set. Set them with `devaudit configure`; author the seed with the e2e-test-data skill.
_comment_e2e_env: Env applied to the E2E setup, (blocking) dev-server, and E2E test steps. To run E2E against a local stack, override EVERY remote/prod key here so production is fully severed — e.g. { "E2E_LOCAL": "1", "NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL": "http://127.0.0.1:54321", "SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY": "<local-service-key>", "RESEND_API_KEY": "re_e2e_local_dummy_key" }. Step-level env wins over the job-level secrets. Values may reference repo secrets, e.g. "${{ secrets.E2E_ADMIN_USERNAME }}". Workflows read repository-level secrets and variables only (not ones that exist only inside a GitHub environment); a name that does not exist reads as empty, and the generated workflows fail before the dev server starts naming each empty one (#1160). Write "${{ secrets.NAME || '' }}" for a value that may be empty.
_comment_e2e_regression: Opt-in: generates e2e-regression.yml, a three-tier smoke/critical/regression E2E gating workflow distinct from the blocking smoke gate above — PR-to-main runs the `critical` Playwright project, a successful production deployment runs the full `regression` project as a post-merge safety net (auto-files a bug/priority:high issue on failure), and workflow_dispatch supports scoped fix-and-verify iterations. Requires playwright.config.ts to define `smoke`/`critical`/`regression` projects (falls back to `smoke` on PR-to-main if `critical` isn't defined yet). Reuses e2e_env/e2e_setup_command/e2e_port above — no separate config surface. Opt in via `devaudit update --enable-e2e-regression <path>` (devaudit-installer#876) rather than hand-editing this field, or set it directly if hand-editing anyway — see docs/e2e-test-tiers.md#opting-into-the-3-tier-regression-gate. Leave false/absent unless you want the ~55-minute full-regression job (most projects don't).
_comment_e2e_concurrency_group: Optional (devaudit-installer#969). Fixed concurrency group for e2e-regression.yml. Leave empty to keep the default per-workflow-and-ref group (`${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}`, cancelling only on pull_request). Set it (e.g. "uat-e2e-data") when the critical/regression specs mutate a SHARED backend, so PR, workflow_dispatch and post-deploy runs queue instead of overlapping; cancel-in-progress then defaults to false (see e2e_concurrency_cancel_in_progress). GitHub keeps one running and one pending run per group, so a newer queued run replaces an older queued one. See docs/e2e-test-tiers.md.
_comment_e2e_concurrency_cancel_in_progr: Optional. Only used when e2e_concurrency_group is set; default false. Set true to restore cancel-in-progress with the fixed group (cancels the running run when a newer one starts - risky mid-mutation on a shared backend).
_comment_e2e_regression_timeout_minutes: Optional. Job timeout in minutes for e2e-regression.yml (default 55). Raise it if the full regression legitimately takes longer; a hook script cannot raise the job-level ceiling.
_comment_test_tiers: Optional (devaudit-installer#1060). Test tiers use the same names for every runner: smoke (minutes, the app starts and the core path works), critical (smoke plus must-not-break journeys), full (everything in the integration/E2E suite), and the feature scope (tests tagged with the branch's requirement). Each test_tier_* is a single-line shell command run from working_directory by scripts/run-test-tier.sh; test_feature_command takes a {REQ} placeholder. Leave a key unset to keep the runner default: for Playwright the existing smoke/critical/regression projects, for test_runner pytest `pytest -m smoke`, `pytest -m "smoke or critical"`, `pytest` and pytest on the test files that mention the id. Unit tests are not tiered. See docs/e2e-test-tiers.md.
_comment_release_gate: Optional (devaudit-installer#1059). Which E2E tier runs on the PR into the release branch: none, smoke, critical or full. These keys are deliberately not listed below: leave them unset to keep today's behaviour (critical, plus the full regression after the production deploy), and add one only to change it. Choose full to test the release candidate before it ships (slower, the full pack can take about an hour); then set post_deploy_full_regression to false to avoid testing the same commit twice. scheduled_full_regression is a cron expression (e.g. "0 3 * * *") that runs the full regression on the integration branch; scheduled runs are not release evidence. Needs e2e_regression_enabled. Change these with `devaudit configure set`; devaudit doctor reviews the choice. See docs/e2e-test-tiers.md.
_comment_release_branch_required_reviews: Optional (DevAudit-Installer#1116). Approving reviews GitHub requires on the release branch: 0, 1 or 2. Not listed below: leave it unset to keep 1, the value `devaudit install` has always applied. 0 lets the author merge their own release PR (a recorded control gap, for a solo developer). `devaudit install` applies it; `devaudit update` keeps the branch at it, and lowering an existing branch asks for a confirmation. Change it with `devaudit configure set release_branch_required_reviews <0|1|2>`.
_comment_onboarding: Optional (DevAudit-Installer#1116). onboarding_preset (A, B, C, D or custom; a missing key means custom) records the onboarding preset the project chose. compliance_frameworks lists the standards the project needs evidence for (soc-2, iso-27001, iso-29119, gdpr, eu-ai-act; empty for none). Neither is listed below; set them with `devaudit configure set`.
_comment_e2e_data: Optional (DevAudit-Installer#1116, test data). Where the end-to-end tests get their data, and how it is prepared. e2e_data_isolation: none, ephemeral (a fresh database per run), shared_serialised (a shared environment only these tests use, one run at a time) or shared (a shared environment others also use); unset keeps today's behaviour. e2e_seed_paths: files or folders that hold the seed. e2e_reset_command / e2e_preflight_command / e2e_leak_check_command: commands the project owns (reset the data, fail when the seed fixtures are absent, print the number of rows left behind). e2e_max_skipped: most skipped tests a run may have. feature_e2e_projects: Playwright projects the feature run uses (unset runs all). e2e_seed_command above keeps its meaning. These are defined now and given behaviour by a later work package; none is listed below. Set them with `devaudit configure set`.
_comment_devaudit: DevAudit destination. base_url lives in git so URL changes are visible in PR review. Falls back to repo Variable DEVAUDIT_BASE_URL if base_url is empty (deprecated in v1.23.0).
_comment_uat: UAT-environment verification (Stage 3 Step 10). Opt-in: enabled=false skips Step 10 entirely. When enabled, only requirements whose risk class is listed in required_risk_classes go through UAT-env verification; use ["*"] to require it for every requirement (projects that UAT every release).
_comment_approval: Release approval policy (Stage 3 Step 11). dual_actor (default) = the approver must differ from the release creator. solo_with_gap = the author may approve their own release; DevAudit records a control gap in compliance/risk-register.md. Nothing approves automatically: an "auto_low_risk" mode is not implemented, so it is not offered, and auto_low_risk_threshold below is unused. Change it with `devaudit configure set approval.mode <value>`; the portal has its own approval policy, which `devaudit doctor` compares with this one.
_comment_commit_validation: validate-commits.sh declared exemptions (devaudit-installer#966). legacy_non_conventional lists commits that predate the Conventional Commits rule and cannot be rewritten: [{"sha": "<7+ hex chars>", "reason": "<why>"}]. Each entry needs a reason, is printed as EXEMPT on every run, and exempts only the format check (requirement traceability still applies). Empty by default.
_comment_production_review: Post-deploy production review gate (Stage 5). terminal_status='prod_review' (default, Option A) means post-deploy-prod.yml stops at prod_review; a human in the portal clicks 'Approve Production' (→ prod_approved) then 'Mark as Released' (→ released) for an explicit two-event audit trail. terminal_status='released' (Option B) preserves the v1.21.x auto-release behaviour — workflow PATCHes straight to released with no human click. Closes #138.
_comment_requirements_aligner: requirements-aligner skill toggles (DevAudit-Installer#119, v0.1.42+). Controls when the skill blocks vs advises. block_on_stage_1=false (default) means the skill advises on AC-to-SRS mapping at plan APPROVAL but doesn't block; flip to true once docs/SRS.md is populated enough for the check to be reliably surfacing real drift (not false-positives on sparse SoT). block_on_stage_3=true means the per-REQ srs-alignment.md artefact is required before Stage 3 completes — the per-REQ evidence is the hard gate. auto_file_followup_issue=false means the skill never opens GitHub issues automatically; if gaps are detected and operator defers, operator files follow-up manually. ramp_up_runs=5 means the first 5 invocations on a project are audit-only regardless of block_on_stage_1, so legacy projects with sparse SRS get time to populate before blocking enforces.
_comment_adr_author: adr-author skill toggles (DevAudit-Installer#120, v0.1.43+). The skill applies a decision tree at Stage 1 plan APPROVAL to judge ADR-worthiness, drafts docs/ADR/ADR-NNN-<slug>.md when warranted, and drops compliance/evidence/REQ-XXX/architecture-decision.md at Stage 3. block_on_stage_1=false (default) means advisory-with-strong-recommend in v1; flip to true once the project's calibrated on the heuristic. block_on_stage_3=true means the per-REQ architecture-decision.md artefact is the hard gate. file_paths_signal_architecture lists path prefixes that should trigger an ADR-worthy verdict when touched — defaults cover lib/services/, lib/repositories/, prisma/schema.prisma, infra/; add project-specific load-bearing paths.
_comment_risk_register_keeper: risk-register-keeper skill toggles (DevAudit-Installer#121, v0.1.44+). The skill maintains compliance/risk-register.md as the project-spanning risk SoT. At Stage 1 (MEDIUM/HIGH risk classifications only by default — LOW skipped) it identifies risks the change introduces, allocates RISK-NNN per project, drafts canonical rows, and injects the reference list into the implementation plan. On incident close it drafts the residual-risk entry. At Stage 3 it drops compliance/evidence/REQ-XXX/risk-assessment.md. For solo_with_gap approval projects it enforces the documented control-gap entry. block_on_stage_1=false (default) means advisory in v1. block_on_stage_3=true means the per-REQ risk-assessment.md artefact is the hard gate. scoring='likelihood-impact' = default 3x3 matrix per 0-project-setup.md (CVSS deferred). stage_1_min_risk_class='MEDIUM' = LOW REQs skip the Stage-1 hook (orchestrator's classification already decided no register entry is warranted).
